faq.q: Why do sloths have such long claws?
faq.a: Their claws are 8 to 10 centimetres long and curved like hooks. They hang over branches so the sloth's weight is held by the hooks, not by squeezing, and they make good defence too.

faq.q: Why don't a sloth's organs squash its lungs?
faq.a: In three-toed sloths, fibrous attachments fix the stomach and liver to the lower ribs. When the sloth hangs upside down the organs stay in place instead of pressing on the lungs.
asks: How do sloths breathe upside down?
Does hanging upside down hurt a sloth?

faq.a: Sloths live on leaves, which are low in energy and slow to digest. Moving slowly, keeping little muscle and letting their body cool saves energy, and slow movement also makes them hard for eagles and jaguars to notice.
asks: Why do sloths move so little?

faq.q: Do sloths ever come down from the trees?
faq.a: About once a week a sloth climbs down to the ground to poo, a risky trip that scientists are still trying to explain. Otherwise they stay up in the trees.
asks: Do sloths live on the ground?

faq.a: Yes, surprisingly well. Sloths paddle with their long arms, and their gas-filled stomach helps them float, so they can cross rivers.

facts: Three-toed sloths have fibrous attachments that anchor the stomach and liver to the lower ribs (Cliffe and colleagues, 2014).
A sloth may take weeks to digest a single meal of leaves.
